To be honest I am a bit dubious of this type of threat. There has been quite a bit of work over the last 20 or so years to update transient protection on most electronic devices. It would be possible to knock out almost any device if the energy density is high enough to overpower transient protection or if the frequency components of the transients are fast enough to get past the protection. The problem is that radiated power is a square root of the distance, and the higher the frequency the more power you need in the signal to get good transmission over physical media such as wires. We also have good redundancy and backup to most infrastructure. To even bring the power grid down for example you would have to have a distributed attack of several EMP bombs at several critical locations, and even then most power would probably be back up within a week or two.
